newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian manufacturing wages rise four pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian manufacturing wages rise four pct.

text.p: Manufacturers in Australia's most populous state, New South Wales (NSW), have been granting wage increases of four percent in the last year, excluding the petroleum industry, a survey has found.
The Australian Business Chamber survey of 500 NSW manufacturers found that the petroleum industry paid increases of apprxoimately five percent in the last year.

Larger manufacturers, those with more than 500 employees, have been paying annual wage increase of approximately five percent in the past year, while small and medium sized manufacturers, those with less than 500 employees, had been paying wage rises of four percent.

While more than 50 percent of all small and medium manufacturers said the wages growth was either matched or exceeded by productivity growth, the figure dropped to 45 percent for larger manufacturers with more than 500 employees.

There was no one particular factor determining wage increases in the manufacturing sector, rather a number of factors including past and present productivity, profits, improved trust and communcitation, the cost of living, indusrty wages and union pressure, the survey found.
Wage increases were also found to be dependent on achieving identified targets or changes in work practices.
The survey found that most employers reviewed the wages of their non-managerial staff between July and September each year.
